channel.title: Climate Errata: register
channel.description: New and updated entries in the Climate Errata register

item.title: [Acknowledged] E-OBS v34.0e precipitation, Greece 2005–2014
item.description: Public ECA&D Greek stations with near-complete years fall from about 10 to 1–2 in 2005–2013 and return to 5–7 from 2014. E-OBS Greek precipitation drops by about 35–45% over exactly those years against both CPC Unified (ratio 0.71–0.83 → 0.40–0.60 → 0.60–0.84) and GPCP (0.55–0.66 → 0.32–0.48 → 0.56–0.79). In 2006 E-OBS has 239 mm over the box, against 599 mm (CPC) and 736 mm (GPCP).

item.title: [Confirmed] NASA MERRA-2 corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) over Australia
item.description: About a 20% dry step from 2016 in PRECTOTCORR over Australia, inherited from the CPC Unified gauge analysis (CPCU) that MERRA-2 uses to correct land precipitation. CPCU's own gauge-count field shows Australia lost about 95% of its gauges in two steps (2007–08 and 2015–16, e.g. E Australia ~590 → 90). GPCP and GPCC do not show the step, and a gauge-independent reanalysis (NCEP R1) confirms it sits in CPCU.

item.title: [Reported (open)] lmoments3 1.0.8 (Ouranos; L-moment engine behind xclim PWM fits) and standard_precip SPI
item.description: Wakeby distribution: quantile/CDF/PDF use the scale-dependent γ unscaled and reject valid δ<0, so 77–85% of fitted 100-yr values are NaN or off by ~50×; standard_precip SPI with dist_type='wak' inherits it (half of months NaN, 78% 'severe drought' vs 5%)

item.title: [Confirmed] Hugonnet et al. 2021, Nature (accelerated global glacier mass loss, 2000–2019)
item.description: The 95% interval on the mass-loss acceleration (48 ± 16 Gt/yr per decade) was formed by doubling a 1σ interval from a regression with ~2 degrees of freedom; the correct t-based 95% half-width is ~1.64× larger (about ±26). The acceleration remains significant at the corrected level; the author notes conservative assumptions elsewhere (temporal decorrelation, density conversion) likely offset the narrower interval.

item.title: [Acknowledged] E-OBS v34.0e precipitation, northern Morocco from February 2006
item.description: Every Moroccan precipitation station in E-OBS within 34–39°N, 10–3.5°W stops on 7 February 2006 (Tangier airport, Al Hoceima, Taza and Rabat-Salé); afterwards the only station on the African side is Ceuta, and the Moroccan grid cells are filled from distant stations. From then on those cells change character while the Iberian cells do not: their October–March maximum daily rainfall (box mean) averages 33 mm in the 2000s, 48 mm in the 2010s and 55 mm in the 2020s (Iberian cells 23, 27, 29 mm), and their E-OBS ensemble spread on wet days rises from 5.3–6.1 mm before 2005 to 6.9–8.0 mm, while Iberia's falls. The Moroccan cells carry about half of the rainfall-extremes trend over the box used by World Weather Attribution Report No. 83. Whether rainfall over northern Morocco really changed cannot be told from E-OBS after 2006.

item.title: [Fixed – released] RTE+RRTMGP radiation code (CESM3, E3SM, ICON)
item.description: 6 interpolation/indexing bugs, all now fixed; the worst (#425, in every release since v1.0) is triggered when a key gas is zero or near zero: the gas keeps absorbing, so runs that remove a gas (for example CO2-removal experiments, or configurations that switch a gas off) understate its effect by 70–80%.
